summary: Risk-Scoped Merge Authority (RMA/v1). Merge authorization is determined by what a diff TOUCHES, not by a lane manifest tier. A diff that touches no reserved surface is authorized on green CI. A diff that touches a reserved surface requires an explicit human approval artifact from a CODEOWNERS member. Fail-closed: anything unclassifiable is treated as reserved.

approval.label: griff-approved
approval.note: Both a label and a head-SHA-bound pm-verdict/v1 APPROVED comment from a CODEOWNERS member are required for a reserved diff. Either alone is insufficient.

surfaces.reserved: Production DDL and production data deletion
Activating member delivery, or weakening the delivery kill switch
surfaces.note: distribution-service.ts carries GOVERNANCE_BRAKE_SOURCES and the routing/gating decision that determines whether anything reaches a member at all. It is reserved for that gate, not for its size.

surfaces.reserved: Worker delivery implementation, for as long as production containment is mandated
surfaces.note: Scoped to containment, not permanent. While containment holds, the worker is the code path between the outbox and a real member, and the exactly-one-DeliveryOutcome invariant is enforced here rather than by any downstream check. Retire this surface when containment is lifted -- see docs/05_operations/RUNTIME_MODE_CONTRACT.md.
surfaces.excludeNote: A test file cannot deliver to a member. Reserving the worker's tests would price writing a regression test at the same attention as changing the delivery path, which is exactly the incentive that makes people stop writing them.

surfaces.reserved: Authentication and authorization authority -- who may act, and as whom
surfaces.note: A weakened authz check is invisible in green CI: the tests that would catch it are the same tests the change edits. This is the one surface where 'the suite passed' is the least informative signal.

surfaces.excludeNote: Committed templates carry variable NAMES, not values. Reserving them would price a documentation edit at the same attention as a credential rotation, which is how a control loses its meaning.

surfaces.reserved: Pricing, member tier authority, and paid provider / subscription spend commitments
Production containment posture while containment is mandated
Merge authority itself — the gates, the machinery that produces required checks, the merge wrapper, ownership, and this file
surfaces.note: A PR must never be able to widen its own authority. This surface is what makes RMA non-self-amending. Branch protection binds CONTEXT NAMES, not workflows, and a same-repo PR runs its own copy of any workflow it edits: with `checks: write` that copy can mint a newer, successful check run under a required name. So every workflow is reserved, not only the three that legitimately produce those contexts. The merge wrapper is reserved for the mirror-image reason: the trusted wrapper would happily merge a change that makes the next wrapper authorize unconditionally. The reserved chain's shared output helper (scripts/ops/shared.ts) is reserved for the same reason: pre-merge-authorization hands its receipt object to emitJson and only then derives an exit code from that same mutable object, so an unreserved change there can rewrite an authorization decision without touching a reserved file.

contentRules.reserved: Destructive SQL anywhere in the diff, regardless of file location
Merge-wrapper entrypoint — repointing the sanctioned merge command is a merge-authority change
contentRules.note: package.json is edited by almost every PR (wiring a new test into test:ops), so reserving the whole file would make RMA meaningless. Only lines that define or repoint the merge commands are reserved. JSON permits escapes inside a string ("ops\u003amerge-wrapper" decodes to the key pnpm runs), so each added line is also matched in its escape-decoded form.

contentRules.reserved: Redefinition of a script key that the required `verify` check invokes — repointing one removes a control without touching a reserved file
contentRules.note: `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs `pnpm verify:static`, `pnpm test:command-center` and `pnpm ci:db-client-boundary` inside the required `verify` job, and `verify:static` fans out to lint / type-check / build / test. Those aggregator keys are read out of the PR's OWN package.json, so a diff that repoints one to `true` would pass a green but empty required check. They are frozen; the leaf `test:<group>` keys are NOT, because wiring a new test file into a group is the ordinary case that RMA exists to keep automatic.

contentRules.reserved: A `test:*` group redefined to a command that runs no test runner
contentRules.note: The complement of ci-required-check-entrypoints. Adding or removing files in a group's `tsx --test` list stays `auto` — that is ordinary wiring and the change is legible in the diff. Replacing the whole value with something that invokes no runner (`true`, `echo skipped`, `exit 0`) empties a group while the required check stays green, so it is reserved. Residual, accepted deliberately: a diff can still delete individual files from a group's list and remain `auto`.

scopeNote: Risk-scoped, not the old tier list under a new name. A path is reserved because a wrong change to it costs money, leaks credentials, reaches members, destroys production data, or removes a control -- not because it used to be Tier C. Pure logic that CI can judge (packages/domain, packages/contracts, scoring, lifecycle repositories) is deliberately NOT reserved: reserving it made every PR a human relay, which is what priced the real decisions at zero attention.

bootstrap.note: Two-phase rollout. Merge Gate and Executor Result Validation load this policy and scripts/ops/merge-authority.cjs from the PR's BASE checkout, so neither can read them until they exist on main. PHASE 1 is the single PR that first lands them: on that PR the base checkout has no classifier, so both gates take their documented bootstrap path and reserve the merge as `human` -- the most restrictive outcome, clearable only by the ordinary reserved-surface artifacts (CODEOWNERS label + head-bound pm-verdict/v1), never by a repo-owner override of a required check. PHASE 2 is every PR after that one: base carries the classifier and the bootstrap path is unreachable. Re-entering PHASE 1 would require deleting merge-authority.cjs from main, which is itself a change to the merge-authority surface and therefore requires a human.
